html:
The Hijra was the move of the prophet Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina in 622. The word means "migration" in Arabic. The year it took place became year one of the Islamic calendar.

In Mecca, Muhammad's preaching of one God had angered the town's leading families. His followers were mocked, boycotted and some were beaten. In 619 he lost his wife Khadija and his uncle Abu Talib, who had protected him, and his position became dangerous.

Help came from Yathrib, an oasis town to the north, torn by feuds between its tribes. Men from Yathrib met Muhammad during the pilgrimage, accepted Islam and invited him to come as a leader and peacemaker.

  • His followers left Mecca first, in small groups.
  • Muhammad left last, with his friend Abu Bakr. Tradition says they hid in a cave for three days while the Meccans hunted them.
  • In Yathrib he was welcomed, and the town became known as Medina, "the city" of the Prophet.

In Medina, Muhammad was no longer a persecuted preacher but the head of a community. He built the first mosque and set out the rights and duties of Muslims, Jews and others in the Constitution of Medina. From this base he fought Mecca and, by 630, won it.

Some years later, the caliph Umar chose the Hijra as the start of the Muslim calendar, a sign that Muslims saw it, not Muhammad's birth or first revelation, as the founding of their community.
sum: The Hijra was the move of the prophet Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina in 622. The word means "migration" in Arabic. The year it took place became year one of the Islamic calendar.
